A TI-84 Graphing Calculator is required.
courses.prerequisites: Algebra I, Algebra II, For Early College, per WMCC, Quantitative Reasoning is recommended, but not necessary
courses.provider: White Mountains Community College (Early College at Your High School)
courses.notes: Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. Level 4 (Early College). Catalog's approved list (p.20) maps it to WMCC MATH214W, 4 credits.

courses.description: This course covers three major modules: ● Music Theory/Songwriting - students will gain an understanding of the fundamental building blocks of music. They will learn how to read rhythms and notes, as well as building chords, writing melodies and composing their own music. ● World Music - students will gain an understanding of music in different world cultures. They will understand how music is important in different communities and gain hands-on experience playing the music in an authentic fashion. ● Music in Media - students will learn how to create music for various forms of media, including movies, video games, and advertisements. They will gain an understanding of techniques used to engage an audience and play with their emotions.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: Adapted Physical Education is an academic course designed to expose students to various activities and sports (at an adapted level based on the student’s needs) that promote an active, healthy lifestyle as well as are aligned with the Society for Health and Physical Education (SHAPE) academic standards. Students will explore the history, strategies, skills and rules of various recreational activities such as: Locomotor, Spatial awareness, sports skills, and health related fitness. Other sports and activities may be introduced as time, equipment and class size allow. Also, students will understand and employ ways to improve health related physical fitness. Students will become familiar with the components of health-related physical fitness which include cardiovascular endurance, flexibility, body composition and muscular strength and endurance. The “Fitnessgram”or (Brockport Fitness test) battery of tests and various technology products will be used to let students self-assess their health related fitness levels on a monthly basis. Students will be expected to dress in appropriate clothing for physical activities unless otherwise directed by the instructor. Most units will entail some skills recognition assessments, written assessments. Other assignments may include: Internet research, fitness journaling, and best course of action mini-reports related to the PE subject area. Class participation, social maturity and a positive attitude are paramount for being successful in this class. Outside class work will be 3hrs. per week maximum. “Fitness for Life, 6th ed.” will be furnished by the instructor so students can refer to them for clarification and to study for written assessments if appropriate with the students’ needs. If a student could not perform book work, alternate cognitive assignments will be created based on the level of the student.
courses.prerequisites: Be recommended by a Case Manager, Specialist, or Director of Student Services
courses.notes: Level listed: Modified (Level 2).

courses.description: Adapted Physical Education 2 is an academic course that builds on mastering the SHAPE standards indicated in APE - I as well as the principles, strategies and teachings learned in Adapted Physical Education 1. Outside class work for this particular course will be no more than 3 hours per week. Unit study guides and a textbook entitled Aerobic Fitness Everyone will be furnished by the instructor so students can refer to them for clarification and to study for written assignments. If a student could not perform book work, alternate cognitive assignments will be created based on the level of the student. All course materials will be adapted based on the class, or the individual student.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of Adaptive PE I, or be recommended by a Case Manager, Specialist, or the Director of Student Services
courses.notes: Level listed: Modified (Level 2).

courses.description: Fitness students will learn about physical fitness, the important role that exercise plays in our lives and how we can safely incorporate exercise into our daily routine. Concepts covered are related to nutrition, proper stretching and cooling down, strength and cardiovascular training, prevention and first aid for sports injuries, and fitness for special populations.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of PE I or equivalent
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard). The course-selection lists (pp.28-31) call it 'Personal Fitness/Sports Skills & Recreational Activities'.

courses.description: Physical Education is an academic course designed to expose students to various activities and sports (at an intermediate level) that promote an active, healthy lifestyle as well as are aligned with the Society for Health and Physical Education (SHAPE) academic standards. Students will explore the history, strategies, skills and rules of various recreational sports such as: Ultimate Frisbee, team handball, archery, orienteering, badminton, Pickleball and volleyball. Other sports and activities may be introduced as time, equipment and class size allow. Also, students will understand and employ ways to improve health related physical fitness. Students will become familiar with the components of health-related physical fitness which include cardiovascular endurance, flexibility, body composition and muscular strength and endurance. The “Fitnessgram” battery of tests and various technology products will be used to let students self-assess their health-related fitness levels on a monthly basis. Students will be expected to dress in appropriate clothing for physical activities unless otherwise directed by the instructor. Most units will entail some skills recognition assessments, written assessments and group project work. Other assignments may include: Internet research, fitness journaling, and best course of action papers related to the PE subject area. Class participation, social maturity and a positive attitude are paramount for being successful in this class. Outside class work will be 3 hours per week maximum. Unit study guides and a textbook entitled “Fitness for Life” will be furnished by the instructor so students can refer to them for clarification and to study for written assessments.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard). Course-selection lists (p.28) show PE I as the required freshman physical education course. A PE II is named in the selection lists (pp.28-31) but has no entry in the course offerings.

courses.description: Students who enroll in this course will be expected to have an independent focus on mastering various SHAPE academic standards through some of the following suggested options: ● Tae-Kwon-Do ● Attend Basic Training (if joining the military) ● Dance lessons ● Weight-lifting The above options would be graded on a pass/fail basis; no number grade will be recorded. Activity type and duration of participation in activity will require verification from an approved course mentor. This course requires the student to develop a learning contract and design an independent project, and in some cases identify a member of the community to work with. This contract requires the approval of the PE teacher and the principal
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of PE I or 1 transfer credit from another school
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard). Independent study.

courses.description: Sports Skills and Recreational Activities is an academic course designed to afford students the opportunity to engage in and study various skills for sports and lifetime recreational activities. Students will explore the history, strategies, skills, and rules of various recreational sports such as: Ultimate Frisbee, team handball, basketball, football, badminton, Pickleball, volleyball, pillo-polo/field hockey, and soccer. Other sports and activities may be introduced as time, equipment, and class size allow. Students will be expected to work towards improving skills in all sports studied, as well as designing and running class tournaments. Students will experience opportunities that promote physical literacy and lifetime wellness. Some units will be delivered by the instructor to the students via NFHSLEARN.COM and others will be study guides furnished by the instructor so students can refer to them for clarification and to study for written assessments.
courses.prerequisites: Successful completion of PE I or equivalent
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: Modified & Standard: Biology is the study of all living things, how they are different, reproduce, grow and live in their surroundings. Weekly laboratory activities will be conducted to reinforce topics studied in the classroom. Honors: This biology class is for students who are considering attending a two or four-year post-secondary institution. Topics of study include biochemistry, genetics, evolution, and ecology. Weekly laboratory experiments will be conducted to reinforce lecture topics.
courses.prerequisites: Modified & Standard: None; Honors: B or higher in Conceptual Physics and Conceptual Chemistry, Algebra I, and instructor's permission
courses.fulfills_text: This is a Required Course; Physics, Chemistry, and Biology are required for graduation (starting with Class of 2027)
courses.notes: Levels listed: Modified (Level 2), Standard (Level 2), Honors (Level 3). Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission for Early College)'; the course-selection lists (pp.29-31) also show Biology for incoming sophomores.

courses.description: Conceptual is designed to introduce students to key topics in chemistry; providing them with a foundation for future science courses. Conceptual Chemistry differs from a more traditional chemistry course in that the focus is on chemical concepts and qualitative laboratory analysis. The goals of Conceptual Chemistry are to develop a conceptual framework for modern chemistry and to allow students to gain experience and appreciation of chemistry through experimentation and inquiry. Students in this course will learn practical scientific skills used to investigate and explore the modern world.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: Practical chemistry is a course that will demonstrate the vital role chemistry plays in everyday life. Students will learn about matter and its properties, the atom, the periodic table, chemical reactions and acids and bases through hands-on activities and real-life examples. Because chemistry can be abstract, this course will use concrete applications to help students comprehend the hypothetical. Students will develop problem-solving skills through the application of chemical concepts to real-world situations.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: Conceptual Physics is an introductory science course designed to prepare students for all future high school science courses. Physics is the basic science. It is the foundation for all other sciences. Since individuals are forced to interact with the physical world around them daily, they need to understand the rules of nature that govern their physical world. While the rules of nature are often described mathematically, it is not the only way to describe them. Conceptual Physics emphasizes learning the fundamental principles of nature from which these concepts are derived. For example, mathematics is not necessary to understand that energy is neither created nor destroyed. This concept is one of the fundamentals of physics. In this course, the focus will be on concepts, ideas, and scientific thinking rather than on high level mathematics. A student only needs to have basic math skills to be successful in this course. Therefore, at the completion of Conceptual Physics, students will have a strong foundational knowledge of the laws that govern the universe and how to apply them to everyday situations.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: Practical physics is a course that will focus on exploring the laws of physics in the context of everyday life and experiences. It will help students understand the fundamental concepts of speed, velocity, acceleration, forces, motion, work, power, and energy and how they apply to their daily lives. Hands-on activities and labs will be used to reinforce and illustrate these concepts and provide students with a deeper understanding of them. This course will focus on using critical thinking skills to help students develop a qualitative understanding of physics rather than focusing on complex mathematical formulas.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.course_name: EC Dendrology & Introduction to Tree and Shrub Identification
courses.description: Dendrology is the study of trees and other woody plants. In Dendrology and Introduction to Tree and Shrub Identification, students learn the taxonomy, geographic range, natural history, ecological relationships, and uses of major tree and shrub families found in New England. Laboratory work focuses on the morphology and classification of common New England trees and shrubs. In the field, the emphasis is on identification. This course is an embedded year-long course within the Diversified Agriculture and Natural Resources program.
courses.provider: White Mountains Community College (Early College at Your High School)
courses.notes: Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. Level 4 (Early College). Catalog's approved list (p.19) maps it to WMCC FRST101W, 4 credits.

courses.description: Forestry Resources introduces students to a wide range of issues that forests face in a changing climate with a growing human population. These interactions between humans and forests are extensive. Humans place significant pressures on forest resources, expecting many services in return. This course explores these interactions and other forestry-related topics, including distribution and forest ecology, silvics and forest management, and ecosystem services. This course also addresses alternative uses for forests and solutions to forestry-related issues. This course is an embedded year-long course within the Diversified Agriculture and Natural Resources program.
courses.prerequisites: WMCC recommends Dendrology & Intro to Tree & Shrub Identification
courses.provider: White Mountains Community College (Early College at Your High School)
courses.notes: Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. Level 4 (Early College). Catalog's approved list (p.20) maps it to WMCC FRST205W, 4 credits.

courses.description: In this course students will acquire the skills and knowledge necessary to become responsible and effective citizens and consumers in an interdependent world. Civics topics covered include the American government, political parties, law, crime and punishment, and citizenship. Economic topics include supply and demand, businesses and the stock market, value and exchange systems, and others. Grades will be based on quizzes, exams, research-based projects, presentations, and general class work.
courses.prerequisites: At least two social studies credits (including Early U.S. History)
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: This course is designed to focus on events from US history from the pre-Columbian era to the conclusion of the Civil War and Reconstruction. The course emphasizes how European contact with the New World shaped the development of cultural, economic, and political institutions from colonial times to the present. Also of importance is the coming of the revolution and the consolidation of the republic, the expansion of democracy, and westward movement across the country. Students are expected to participate fully in class through note taking, discussion, and classwork assignments. Grades will be based on quizzes, exams, research projects, presentations, general coursework, and participation.
courses.prerequisites: World History or World Events and Geography (or equivalent 1 credit course)
courses.notes: Levels listed: Standard (Level 2), Honors (Level 3). U.S. History is required for graduation.

courses.description: This course will chart the history of the United States from the end of the Civil War to the dawn of the twenty-first century. Major themes include migrations to and within the country, economic transformations, the rise of the US as a world power, the evolution of the role of the federal government, and the long struggle for individual and group rights. The course strives to understand these changes and conflicts through the perspective of a variety of people’s everyday experiences and concerns.
courses.prerequisites: World History or World Events and Geography and Early US History
courses.notes: Levels listed: Standard (Level 2), Honors (Level 3). U.S. History is required for graduation.

courses.description: This course is a broad introduction to the field of psychology. Students will explore the key figures, diverse theoretical perspectives, and research findings that have shaped some of the major areas of contemporary psychology. This course also examines the research methods used by psychologists across these areas to study the origins and variations in human behavior. Grades will be based on quizzes, exams, a research project, and general course work.
courses.prerequisites: Earned at least 2 social studies credits. Recommended NWEA reading level of at least 220
courses.notes: Level listed: Honors (Level 3). The course-selection lists call it 'Psychology Honors'.

courses.description: This class is intended as an introductory social studies course with an emphasis on basic social studies knowledge including geography, economics, and causes of conflict. This course will look at world events through the filter of geography using the themes of location, place, movement, human-environmental interaction, and regions. Students will use maps, conduct research, write essays, give presentations, as well as demonstrate geographic understanding through general course work.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard). Entry adds: 'Strongly recommended for Freshman year'.

courses.description: This course will look at world events from the origin of early humans and non-human primates and will end with the Renaissance and Reformation periods. This course will cover evolution, early societies and civilizations, kingdoms and empires, the achievements of the classical world, and the transition into the early modern era. Students’ grades will be based on reading, quizzes, exams, essays, research papers, and other projects.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: Driver’s education is an essential first step to lifelong driving skills and is one of the first major responsibilities in a teenager’s life. This course teaches basic traffic laws, rules of the road, basic motor vehicle operation, driver awareness, and drug and alcohol effects on driving. This course is offered each spring.
courses.prerequisites: Must be 16 years old by June 30 for NH students. Must be 15 years old by April 1 for VT students. VT students must provide their learner’s permit number prior to the start of the course.
courses.notes: Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: This 5-day/week LNA licensure program will take place at the Coos County Nursing Home in West Stewartstown, New Hampshire. Students will be scheduled for their block one class. Students will get 60 hours of theory (lecture), 70 hours of clinical (hands on) for sufficient course hours to test and apply for LNA licensure with the state of New Hampshire. The school district will pay for all costs associated with the course including the workbook, criminal record check, the state exam and licensing fees. The cost of the medical physical is the student’s own responsibility. Students are also responsible for transportation back and forth from the nursing home and school. Enrollment maximums will vary year-to-year. Students from Colebrook Academy and Pittsburg High School participate as well.
courses.prerequisites: Must be 16 years old when the course starts. For acceptance into the program, students must write a short essay on “why I want to be an LNA”; pass a test that indicates ability to read and write English and has decision-making/judgement skills; provide 3 letters of references (unrelated) who can vouch for character, reliability and integrity; have a physical done by a medical provider and undergo a tuberculin skin test.
courses.provider: Coos County Nursing Home, West Stewartstown, New Hampshire
courses.notes: Level listed: Honors (Level 3). Students from Colebrook Academy and Pittsburg High School also participate.

courses.description: This course is recommended for a student interested in enrolling in the Building Trades CTE Program. Through the use of computer-aided drafting, field trips to construction sites and examination of trade journals and drawings, students will learn the varied construction industry. Students will study architectural styles and the evolution of technology in construction. Students will design, estimate and schedule phases of the Building Trades project. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to read and interpret blueprints, understand permits, building codes and develop the skills necessary to plan a building project. The following areas will be emphasized: Project planning; Construction estimating; Heavy equipment / Site selection; Permits / Zoning / Building codes; Architectural drafting; Residential and Commercial construction; Internet resources; Mechanical and Electrical systems.
courses.notes: Pre-Tech Foundation Course for Integrated Trades (subheading). Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: This course is recommended for a student interested in enrolling in the Building Trades CTE program. This course is designed to give students the basic skills necessary to make minor repairs around the home. Through a series of projects and exercises, students will learn the use of portable power tools and hand tools. Students will demonstrate basic knowledge of plumbing and electrical systems in the home. This course will cover topics from changing a furnace filter, sharpening a lawn mower blade to patching holes in drywall. The following areas will be emphasized: Home safety; Portable power and hand tools; Electrical systems; Plumbing and Heating Systems; Painting and interior finishes; Building Materials and fasteners; Weatherization and energy savings. Upon completion of this course, students will have the knowledge of what is necessary to maintain and repair the various systems in a home. Through this course students will be exposed to some of the many trades in the construction industry. Carpenter, Plumber and Electrician are some of the skilled trades students will be introduced to. Students will be graded on bringing a job to completion in an efficient and craftsmen-like matter. It is to be understood that the completed job must be at an industry standard that is to be determined by the instructor. Students are graded along the way to job completion and not just on the finished product. Tasks will be graded during the job process, which includes safety, material use, time management and problem-solving ability. Students will be responsible to follow all class rules and class policy that are distributed at the beginning of the school year and reviewed with the instructor, students and parents. Everyone must recognize that the shop is much different than a classroom and proper attitude must be maintained at all times.
courses.notes: Pre-Tech Foundation Course for Integrated Trades (subheading). Level 2 (Standard). Called 'Home Repair' in the course-selection lists.

courses.description: This course is recommended if a student is interested in enrolling in either the Advanced Integrated Manufacturing or Building Trades Program. This hands-on course is designed to give students the basic skills and knowledge necessary to create a project out of wood. Through a series of projects and lessons, students will learn the use of hand and power tools and finishing methods. The following areas will be emphasized: Shop safety; Machine/Tool safety; Fraction and ruler skills and Creativity.
courses.notes: Pre-Tech Foundation Course for Integrated Trades (subheading). Level 2 (Standard).

courses.description: This hands-on course is a continuation of Woodworking I. In this class, students will learn basic drafting skills to help them read prints and sketch a basic design to create a project out of wood. Students will be required to design and construct their own project. The projects will require more difficult construction methods such as doors & drawers. As in Woodworking I, the following areas will be emphasized: Shop safety; Machine/Tool safety; Fraction and ruler skills; Basic Drafting skills and Creativity.
courses.prerequisites: Woodworking I with an 85 or better (or with instructor approval)
courses.notes: Pre-Tech Foundation Course for Integrated Trades (subheading). Level 2 (Standard). Grade placement is printed '9-012' (typo for 9-12 presumed).

courses.description: This hands-on course is a more detail oriented course in woodworking and a continuation of Woodworking II. Students will be expected to create their own drafted print with sizes and construction methods of an item they will then produce. This item will be a more complex item than in previous courses. Also, students may be required to build and display one item that will be auctioned off at the end of the course. The following areas will still be emphasized: Shop safety; Machine/Tool safety; Fraction and ruler skills; Drafting skills and Creativity.
courses.prerequisites: Woodworking I and II with an 85 or better (or with instructor approval)
courses.notes: Pre-Tech Foundation Course for Integrated Trades (subheading). Level 2 (Standard). The course-selection lists also name a Woodworking IV that has no entry.

courses.description: Students enrolled in this course are provided with an overview instruction with a focus on firefighter personal protective equipment, fire behavior, building construction, fire suppression, EMS culture of safety, patient assessment and treatment skills. Just as in the actual Emergency Services CTE courses, students will learn to demonstrate problem-solving and critical thinking skills to analyze, synthesize and evaluate situations independently and in teams. Students may have the opportunity to earn Wildland Firefighter certification via VT Agency of Natural Resources and the VT Fire Academy. They will also have an introduction to emergency scene management and may have an opportunity to earn National Incident Management Systems certifications. Initial exploration of Emergency Service will include classroom work (lectures, readings, skills, practicals) and visits with local experts in the field. Students may participate in a ride-along with local first responders and fire departments per the authority of the department chief’s permission and school administration
courses.notes: Pre-Tech Foundation Course for Fire & Emergency Services (subheading). Level 2 (Standard). Called 'Intro to Fire & EMS' in the course-selection lists.

courses.description: The Business Administration and Technology (BAT) Program is designed to equip students with the essential knowledge and skills needed for success in today’s competitive business environment. Through a combination of hands-on learning experiences, dual-credit course opportunities, and involvement in real-world business operations, students are prepared to enter the workforce or continue their education at a postsecondary institution with confidence and competence. Students in this program develop a strong foundation in business principles, financial literacy, marketing, entrepreneurship, accounting, and technology applications. They gain practical experience that mirrors real business operations, enhancing their understanding of the professional world and the expectations of today’s employers. A key component of the program is active student participation in the school store, a dynamic, student-run enterprise. This experience gives students first hand exposure to concepts such as cost and profit analysis, customer service, inventory management, accounting, marketing, advertising, and more—valuable skills that translate directly into workplace readiness. Additionally, students become members of Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA), the nation’s premier business career student organization. FBLA’s mission is to inspire and prepare students to become community-minded business leaders in a global society through leadership development, academic competitions, and career preparation events. Whether entering the workforce immediately after high school or pursuing a college degree, graduates of the Business Administration and Technology Program leave with a competitive edge, a professional mindset, and a comprehensive understanding of the business world.
courses.notes: Honors Level (Level 3). Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. CTE program offered by Canaan Schools itself (not a separate CTE center). Two-year program meeting two blocks per day. YEAR 1 (9 college credits): RS Comprehensive Presentation Methods; RS Intro to Business Administration; RS Intro to Business Logic & Ethics; CTSO Membership: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA); School Store/Student Lounge. YEAR 2 (9 college credits): RS Accounting I; RS Marketing; RS Business Software Applications; CTSO Membership: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA); School Store/Student Lounge. Industry Recognized Credentials (IRC's): American Heart Association AED/CPR First Aid Certification; CareerSafe OSHA-10 General Industry Certification; ServSafe Food Handler Certification; Conover Credential Workplace Readiness. program

courses.description: Technical education of Emergency Medical Technicians will include classroom work such as lectures/discussions, text/current on-line curriculum resources, and updated skills/practicals to prepare students for the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians EMT – Basic Level of Care. This credential affords students the ability to work in the patient care setting in an ambulance and or as medical technician at hospital emergency departments. To be eligible to test for the NREMT EMT-B certification, students will earn industry recognized credentials (listed below). Students will be issued their own medical kits to train with to apply skills training and preparation for patient assessment and care for the sick and injured including adults, pediatrics and geriatrics. Students will participate in career specific training with the 45 th EMS and the Upper Connecticut Valley Hospital Emergency Department via professional training preceptor agreements.
courses.fulfills_text: Embedded Credits: 1 Science credit upon completion of program
courses.notes: Honors Level (Level 3). Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. CTE program offered by Canaan Schools itself (not a separate CTE center). One block per day. Dual-Enrollment Opportunities: Emergency Medical Technician Basic (6 credits through NMCC). Industry-Recognized Certifications: American Heart Association Basic Life Support CPR; American Heart Association First Aid Certification; National Incident Management System (NIMS) 100, 200, 700 courses; National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians EMT - Basic Level of Care. This program is now being offered during one block for one year instead of two blocks three times a week for two years. program

courses.description: Technical education of firefighting will include classroom work such as lectures/discussions, text/current on-line curriculum resources, and updated skills/practicals that lead to combined training operations to prepare students for the National Fire Protection Association- Firefighter I credential testing. To be eligible to test for NFPA ProBoard FFI, students will earn industry recognized credentials (listed below). Students will be outfitted with their own personal protective firefighting equipment and will utilize this PPE in all hands-on skills training and preparation for fire and rescue duties, including fire suppression tactics, vehicle and heavy rescue extrication skills, technical rescue skills and hazardous materials emergencies. Live fire training is also mandatory for students seeking a NFPA FFI Credential and will take place in the late spring at the VT Fire Academy in Pittsford, VT. This includes two days of training including interior firefighting, car and dumpster fires as well as roof ventilation operations. Classes may take place at the Beecher Falls Volunteer Fire Department to afford the use of firefighter tools and apparatus for proficient skill building.
courses.fulfills_text: Embedded Credits: 1 Math credit and 1 PE credit upon completion of the two-year program
courses.notes: Honors Level (Level 3). Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. CTE program offered by Canaan Schools itself (not a separate CTE center). One block per day. Industry-Recognized Certifications: American Heart Association Basic Life Support CPR; American Heart Association First Aid; National Fire Protection Association’s Firefighter I; National Incident Management System (NIMS) 100, 200, 700 courses; NFPA ProBoard Hazardous Materials Operations; Traffic Incident Management for First Responders (TIMS); Wildland Firefighting. Note: In 2025-2026, this course will be taught during one block all year instead of two blocks. Therefore, new students in the Fire program will not earn any embedded credits upon completion of the first year. program

courses.description: The Integrated Trades program is a dynamic, hands-on course that merges key elements from the former Building Construction & Restoration Carpentry (BT) and Diversified Agriculture & Natural Resources (DAgNR) programs. Designed to prepare students for entry-level employment or further education, this program provides a comprehensive experience in both the construction and agricultural trades through immersive, real-world learning. Students will engage in every phase of construction work, from deconstruction to finish carpentry, gaining essential job-site experience and learning to navigate building renovations with confidence. In addition to construction, students will explore modern agricultural and natural resource industries. These experiences help students develop entrepreneurial thinking, communication, and decision-making skills. The program takes place almost entirely in a real-world, job site or outdoor setting, such as the Canaan Community Forest, while emphasizing safety, professionalism, and workplace readiness. Students should be prepared to work outdoors in all weather conditions and must have appropriate gear and a strong work ethic. Safety is prioritized in all activities, especially those involving equipment such as chainsaws, tractors, and power tools. Students also have the opportunity to participate in the National FFA Organization, a nonprofit career and technical student organization (CTSO) dedicated to promoting career success for students in the Agriculture, Food, and Natural Resources career cluster. FFA is student-led, dynamic, and determined to help students grow personally, as well as develop critical career and leadership skills. It accomplishes this through national events, programs, contests, and more.
courses.credits_text: 4 per year and 8 college credits upon completion
courses.fulfills_text: Embedded Credits: 1 Math credit and 1 Science credit upon completion of program
courses.notes: Honors Level (Level 3). Grade placement printed as '11-12 (10 with instructor permission)'. CTE program offered by Canaan Schools itself (not a separate CTE center). Two-year program meeting two blocks per day. The following areas are emphasized: Safety; Principles of new construction; Building remodeling and restoration; Carpentry tools and equipment use; Building materials and hardware; Residential plumbing, electrical, heating; Maple syrup production; Sawmill operation; Wreath production; Small animal farming; Basic Logging; Greenhouse Growing. Dual-Enrollment Opportunities: Dendrology and Intro to Tree & Shrub Identification (4 credits); Forestry Resources (4 credits). Industry-Recognized Certifications: OSHA-10; American Heart Association AED/CPR First Aid Certification; Game of Logging (Chainsaw Safety) Levels 1, 2, 3, and 4; Man Lift Certification; National Safe Tractor and Machinery Operation Program (NSTMOP); Powder Actuated Tools Certification; 30-Hour Welding Course through White Mountain Community College. By integrating both construction and natural resource-based trades, the Integrated Trades program offers students a broad skill set and exposure to a wide range of career paths, all taught through experiential, hands-on learning. program

courses.description: Concurrent College and High School Credit Opportunities For Vermont Residents (VT DE) allows high school juniors and seniors to take up to two college courses for free at participating postsecondary partner schools. These classes are weighted as heavier than Honors courses and are designated on transcripts with “DE” at the end of the course name. For example, (CCV) Law Enforcement in America - DE indicates that it was a dual enrollment class through Community College of Vermont (CCV). Students can take courses during the summer of his/her junior year through the spring semester of his/her senior year. The program is only available to students who are Vermont residents. There are currently 19 participating colleges throughout the state. To find out more about this program, see http://www.vtdualenrollment.org. Accommodations are allowable; however, DE coursework cannot be modified. If a student withdraws from a DE course after the add/drop deadline at CMHS but prior to the college’s, the high school will enter a “W” and the course will remain on the high school transcript. Students who withdraw from a DE course will continue in a non-DE version of the course or an alternative option (like an independent study) which will be added to the schedule and transcript for credit. The student will have to complete withdrawal paperwork for the college and the institution will apply an appropriate grade to the student’s college transcript.
courses.provider: Participating Vermont postsecondary partner colleges
courses.notes: program. Eligibility requirements for VT DE: Be enrolled as a junior or senior at CMHS; Be a resident of the State of Vermont; Not have taken more than 2 DE courses (available beginning the summer after the 10th grade year through the 12th grade year of high school); Earn a minimum score of 40 (math), 80 (reading) and 80 (writing) on the Accuplacer Assessment. Certain previous DE or RS courses or the CCV course: Intro to College and Careers may waive this requirement; Students must apply for a free payment voucher.

courses.course_name: Early College at Your High School (EC)
courses.description: The majority of DE opportunities are offered through White Mountain Community College’s (WMCC) Early College at Your High School (EC) program (formerly known as Running Start) through the Community College System of NH (CCSNH). Students receive high school credit for these courses offered at CMHS; however, students must request an official college transcript from the issuing institution to show the college credit. The courses are taught by high school teachers who meet the hiring qualifications for CCSNH faculty, and the course work and materials meet the college level content standards. These classes are weighted as Level 4: Dual Enrollment and are designated on transcripts with “RS”. Students enrolled in an Early College in Your High School course MUST engage in the college’s curriculum; however, the student may elect NOT to earn the college credits. The registration fee for each Early College at Your High School course is $150 and is paid for by the Canaan School District. A student who fails an Early College at Your High School course or withdraws from it after the add/drop deadline will have to reimburse the school district the $150 course fee. At the beginning of the semester, a representative from White Mountains Community College meets with all students scheduled for Early College at Your High School courses and explains the advantages of taking Early College/RS, the registration process, costs, etc.
courses.provider: White Mountains Community College (Early College at Your High School)
courses.notes: program. Eligibility requirements for EC: Be enrolled as a junior or senior at CMHS. Sophomores can participate with approval from the teacher, guidance and college. Approval is based on preparedness for the course content and likelihood of taking additional courses in 11th and/or 12th grade; Maintain an 89 (B) weighted GPA; Receive written approval from the previous year’s content-area teacher; Submit a completed “habits of work” checklist. Approved course lists on pp.18-20: White Mountains Community College (72 possible credits), Central Maine Community College (4), Northern Maine Community College (6); 82 credits total. The EC courses taught at CMHS are extracted as separate records (EC ...).

courses.description: The Fast Forward program allows Vermont residing students in CTE programs to get credit for college courses taken at regional CTE centers. Fast Forward is for Vermont students who have not yet graduated from high school and who are enrolled in a partner career technical education center program. The courses are taught at the regional CTE, and classes are scheduled during the regular school day. Each student is given two courses. Fast Forward helps students get high school and college credits (from either VTC or CCV), earn their degree faster, and start their career sooner. Students must request a voucher in the same way as Dual Enrollment.
courses.provider: Regional CTE centers (college credit from VTC or CCV)
courses.notes: program

courses.description: Some colleges and universities in Vermont have developed an early admission program that allows high school seniors to take a full year of college-level classes while earning their high school diploma. The ECP simultaneously serves as a student's senior year of high school and a full year of college credit. Students enrolled in ECP are not eligible for Valedictorian or Salutatorian status. Students may take a year-long course of study in any discipline. The following have been approved to offer an ECP for the upcoming year: Castleton State University, Community College of Vermont, Goddard College, Johnson State College, Lyndon State College, Norwich University and Vermont Technical College (Vermont Academy of Science and Technology (VAST). For more information, students should contact the approved college directly to apply.
courses.provider: Approved Vermont colleges (Castleton State University, Community College of Vermont, Goddard College, Johnson State College, Lyndon State College, Norwich University, Vermont Technical College)
courses.notes: program

courses.course_name: Virtual Learning Academy Charter School (VLACS) (For New Hampshire Residents)
courses.description: The Virtual Learning Academy Charter School is New Hampshire’s first statewide, online school that is available, free of charge, to all middle and high school students who live in New Hampshire. The Academy also serves out-of-state students on a tuition basis. The Academy has been approved as a public charter school by the New Hampshire Board of Education and is also a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. An independent Board of Trustees governs the school. CMHS’ students who are residents of NH can enroll in a VLACS course at any time during their academic career. Grades earned in VLACS courses are calculated into a student’s GPA based on the level of difficulty indicated by VLACS. Students can elect to take AP courses from VLACS and these would be Honors. Regular VLACS courses and competency courses are Standard. VLACS courses will be noted on students’ schedules and ultimately on their final transcripts. Students taking a VLACS course will be assigned to the library.
courses.provider: VLACS
courses.notes: program

courses.course_name: Early College Online (formerly known as eStart) (For New Hampshire Residents)
courses.description: VLACS also offers some courses as Early College Online through CCSNH. These would be weighted heavier than Honors courses. The cost for these courses is $150. Students can submit receipt of payment to the school district for reimbursement. Monies may also be available to cover the cost of books and/or other materials. A student who fails one of these courses or withdraws from it after the add/drop deadline will have to reimburse the school district the $150 course fee. Early College Online courses produce credits from community colleges around the state. The Early College Online courses produce credits from various NH institutions like White Mountains Community College, New Hampshire Technical Institute and Southern New Hampshire University.
courses.provider: VLACS / Community College System of NH
courses.notes: program

courses.description: Work-based learning experiences are an opportunity for students to apply academic, technical and employability skills in a work setting. These opportunities particularly help students make the connection between academic principles and real-world applications. For many, understanding “Why do I need to know this?” provides motivation for more learning. WBL experiences are available to all students as a way to explore academic and career areas of interests. While WBL experiences are intended to coincide with a CTE program (at which time the grade would be weighted as Honors), they can also be set up in areas of interest outside of a CTE program (at which time the grade would be weighted as Standard). Depending on what tasks and learning objectives are a part of the WBL, students can be paid or not paid for their WBL program. Students and their families will be responsible for transportation to the WBL. Students who are interested in WBL should notify the School Guidance Counselor of his/her intentions when registering for courses in the semester prior to when the internship is to begin. They may work together to identify and secure a WBL site. Prior to beginning the WBL experience, an agreement between the school, the WBL site, the student and parents will be completed and a supervisor at the WBL site identified. WBL will be closely monitored by the School Guidance Counselor. Grades for WBL will be based on weekly activity logs, twice a semester site supervisor evaluations and an online course through VtVLC “Workplace and Internship Readiness”.
courses.notes: program. Grades for WBL are weighted Honors when coinciding with a CTE program, Standard otherwise (per catalog text).

courses.course_name: Virtual High School (VHS) and Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VtVLC)
courses.description: CMHS students have the opportunity to participate in online courses through Virtual High School (VHS) or Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VtVLC). Students can take these online courses for the purposes of enrichment, not to fulfill requirements, unless extenuating circumstances exist. They are assigned to a supervised location and work independently. Courses must be pre-approved by the School Guidance Counselor, who also monitors the course. These courses are typically worth ½ credit. The add/drop period for these courses is the same as a regular course. Freshmen are discouraged from taking online courses due to the need of working independently; however, this will be determined on an individual basis. Also, if a student fails one online class, it is highly likely the student will not be able to take any additional online classes. VHS’ course offerings can be viewed at: https://vm3.vhslearning.org/catalog and VtVLC’s course offerings are located at: https://vtvlc.maestrosis.com/RS_FEViewCourses.aspx.
courses.provider: VHS / VtVLC
courses.notes: program

courses.course_name: Northeast Kingdom Learning Services (NEKLS) & the High School Completion Program (HSCP)
courses.description: HSCP allows our students to carve out their own path to high school graduation by working collaboratively with CMHS and NEKLS, Inc. to create a plan that meets Vermont state graduation requirements as well as individual student goals. Starting with the student’s CMHS’ transcript as a baseline, students can integrate courses, learning competencies, projects, employment, college courses, etc. to ultimately earn their CMHS diploma. To be in the program, students must be at least 16-years-old, pass HSCP testing standards, still be connected academically in some way to CMHS, and be recommended by the school. If a student or the family is interested in HSCP as a means to earn the diploma, a meeting should be scheduled with the School Guidance Counselor to complete a referral form. This form is reviewed and approved by a team which can include the Superintendent, Principal, School Guidance Counselor, Director of Student Services and Learning Plan Manager. Because of the individual nature of these learning plans, it is possible for students to meet their graduation requirements earlier than other seniors in June. If this happens, students are still required to continue any courses at CMHS they are enrolled in. During the time they have been in HSCP, students will work with the School Guidance Counselor to explore and secure a Work-based Learning experience.
courses.provider: NEKLS, Inc.
courses.notes: program
